# oasdiff err-ignore file: each non-comment line is matched as a
# substring against the rendered breaking-change description. Each
# line MUST contain the endpoint identifier (method + path) AND the
# specific change text. Each entry MUST cite the PR that introduced
# it so a future audit can trace the rationale.
#
# Format reference:
# https://github.com/Tufin/oasdiff/blob/main/docs/BREAKING-CHANGES.md

# PR axonflow-enterprise#1764 - SDKCompatInfo schema correction.
# The platform has returned per-language object maps for
# sdk_compatibility.min_sdk_version + recommended_sdk_version since
# v4.8.0 (the same release that introduced the field). All four SDKs
# at v6.0.0+ depend on the object shape - the Go SDK v6.0.0 CHANGELOG
# calls this out explicitly as a wire-shape bug fix. The agent-api.yaml
# string shape was the bug; the platform behaviour is the contract.
# Entries are scoped to those two specific properties so unrelated
# future breaking changes on /health still trip the gate.
GET /health the `sdk_compatibility/min_sdk_version` response's property type/format changed from `string`/`` to `object`/`` for status `200`
GET /health the `sdk_compatibility/recommended_sdk_version` response's property type/format changed from `string`/`` to `object`/`` for status `200`

# PR axonflow-enterprise#2422 - HITL spec path rename.
# The handler has always been at /api/v1/hitl/queue (since v9 Phase 8);
# the spec had drifted to /api/v1/hitl/decisions. Renaming the spec to
# match the handler is a doc-only correction with zero customer impact:
# no SDK consumed the decisions path (it 404'd at runtime), no plugin
# referenced it, and the existing handler paths under /queue/* are
# untouched. Both the path_template lockstep test and the dedicated
# integration tests confirm /queue is what the binary serves.
in API GET /api/v1/hitl/decisions api path removed without deprecation
in API POST /api/v1/hitl/decisions api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /api/v1/hitl/decisions/{id} api path removed without deprecation
in API POST /api/v1/hitl/decisions/{id}/approve api path removed without deprecation
in API POST /api/v1/hitl/decisions/{id}/reject api path removed without deprecation

# PR axonflow-enterprise#2881 (docs session API-1) - agent-api.yaml corrections.
# (a) The /api/v1/accuracy/*, /api/v1/conformity/*, and /api/v1/euaiact/*
# families never existed on the agent (some never existed anywhere); the
# shipped EU-AI-Act surface lives on the orchestrator at
# /api/v1/euaiact/* (ee overlay) and is documented in
# ee/docs/api/eu-ai-act-api.md. Removal is a doc-only correction.
# (b) /mcp/check-input + /mcp/check-output were documented at the wrong
# paths - the handlers have only ever been registered at
# /api/v1/mcp/check-input|check-output (mcp_handler.go:575-576).
# (c) /api/v1/circuit-breaker/activate|deactivate never existed - the
# routes are /trip and /reset (circuitbreaker/handler.go:71-72).
# (d) /decide 429 body is written by the auth middleware (shared
# rate-limit envelope), never the DecideErrorResponse the spec claimed.
# (e) HITL: the handler has always required client_id/original_query/
# request_type/triggered_policy_* /trigger_reason (hitl/service.go:135-160),
# parsed {id} as a UUID, and accepted comma-separated status filters.
# In every case the platform behaviour is the contract; the YAML was the bug.

# PR axonflow-enterprise#2881 - orchestrator-api.yaml corrections.
# (a) /api/v1/media/analyzers*, /api/v1/media/analyze, /api/v1/llm-providers/health,
# and /api/v1/agents/domain/{domain} never existed in any shipped binary
# (zero route registrations; the agents domain handler is dead code, #2884).
# (b) The audit family has always 401'd without X-Tenant-ID
# (run.go:2601-2607, :2684-2696), audit/tool-call has always required the
# X-Axonflow-Proxy-Auth HMAC outside Community (run.go:2767-2785), and the
# unified stream handler has always read X-Org-ID (unified_execution_handler.go:75-98)
# - the spec previously omitted required headers the platform enforced.
# (c) audit/search has always returned {entries,total,limit,offset}
# (run.go:2635-2645), never a bare array.
# (d) /health sdk_compatibility maps: same correction as PR #1764 made for
# agent-api.yaml - per-language object maps since v4.8.0 (capabilities.go:20-23).
in API GET /api/v1/agents/domain/{domain} api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /api/v1/audit/tenant/{tenant_id} added the new required `header` request parameter `x-tenant-id`
in API GET /api/v1/llm-providers/health api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /api/v1/media/analyzers api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /api/v1/media/analyzers/{name}/health api path removed without deprecation
in API GET /api/v1/unified/executions/{id}/stream added the new required `header` request parameter `x-org-id`

# v9.8.0 (#2890): euaiact/export is now documented as a thin PROXIED pointer in
# agent-api.yaml - the canonical request/response contract lives in
# orchestrator-api.yaml (per the single-entry-point Option-C convention). The full
# request body + response schema were intentionally moved to the orchestrator spec;
# the agent-api entry is a reachability pointer. The endpoint itself is unchanged
# (still POST → 202 async, proxied to the orchestrator). Ignore vs the v9.7.0 mirror
# baseline, which carried the fully-inlined shape.
in API POST /api/v1/euaiact/export removed the request body
in API POST /api/v1/euaiact/export removed the success response with the status `200`

# PR axonflow-enterprise#3099 (#3066 C3-3) - RBI audit-export scope binding.
# X-Org-ID was already mandatory on these five operations at runtime before the
# spec caught up: the AxonFlow Agent gateway Set()s the header from the
# validated client credential on every /api/v1/rbi request, and the orchestrator
# now fails closed (401) without it. The in-repo example clients DO set the
# header (go, python, typescript, java), but no client can rely on its own
# value: the agent gateway Set()s X-Org-ID from the validated credential on
# every /api/v1/rbi request, overwriting whatever the caller sent. So the
# parameter becoming required is not breaking for any real caller.
# any client-provided value. The parameter is therefore "newly required" only in
# the document; nothing that reaches these routes can break. The companion
# removal of the `?org_id=` query parameter is the security fix itself (it let a
# caller select another organization's exports) and lands as a WARN, not an ERR.
in API GET /api/v1/rbi/audit-exports added the new required `header` request parameter `x-org-id`
in API POST /api/v1/rbi/audit-exports added the new required `header` request parameter `x-org-id`
in API GET /api/v1/rbi/audit-exports/{export_id} added the new required `header` request parameter `x-org-id`
in API DELETE /api/v1/rbi/audit-exports/{export_id} added the new required `header` request parameter `x-org-id`
in API POST /api/v1/rbi/audit-exports/{export_id}/process added the new required `header` request parameter `x-org-id`

# PR axonflow-enterprise#3248 (#3246) - SEBI export-status 200 removal.
# The route queried `sebi_audit_exports`, a table that appears in NO migration
# in this repository and that nothing has ever written to, so the documented
# 200 was unreachable: every call returned 500 on every deployment, always. It
# survived because its only tests were sqlmock tests supplying rows for a table
# that cannot exist. Removing a success status that could never be produced
# breaks no caller - there was no caller, and the UI's getSEBIExportStatus has
# no call site. The route now returns 501 naming the endpoint that does this job
# (POST /api/v1/compliance/reports). Scoped to this one operation so any other
# success-status removal still trips the gate.
in API GET /api/v1/sebi/audit/export/{export_id} removed the success response with the status `200`

# PR axonflow-enterprise#3429 (#3424) - avg_latency_ms becomes nullable.
# This is a deliberate, consumer-visible contract change, not a doc
# correction, and it is recorded here rather than avoided because the
# alternative is worse: the field was a non-nullable number produced by
# COALESCE(AVG(...), 0), so "no row in this range carried a measurement"
# and "the measured average was zero" were the same value on the wire.
# The portal rendered that as a confident "Avg Latency: 0ms" on a stack
# that had just enforced real governed traffic. A number that cannot
# express "unknown" cannot be corrected without becoming nullable.
# Impact is bounded and checked: the ONLY consumer of POST
# /api/v1/audit/report in this org is the Enterprise customer portal
# (ee/platform/customer-portal-ui getAuditReport, proxied via
# orchestrator_proxy_allowlist.go:90), which ships in lockstep with the
# orchestrator and is updated in this PR; no SDK, example or plugin
# reads it. A client that cannot accept null can key on the new
# latency_sample_count (0 exactly when the average is null) instead of
# on the value. #3254 is the standing task for auditing SDK models
# against these specs; the companion /api/v1/audit/summary change is
# additive (the property was undocumented there) and raises no ERR.
in API POST /api/v1/audit/report the response property `avg_latency_ms` became nullable for the status `200`

# PR axonflow-enterprise (#3433) - session-summary avg_latency_ms becomes
# nullable, completing the #3424 family.
# Same deliberate, consumer-visible contract change as the #3429 entry above,
# for the same reason: the field was a non-nullable number produced by
# COALESCE(AVG(...), 0), so "no row in this bucket carried a measurement" and
# "the measured average was zero" were one value on the wire. Whole planes
# record no duration by design (HITL approvals, workflow lifecycle rows, the
# connector-exec MCP closure #3432), so the absent case is the NORMAL one here,
# not an edge. A number that cannot express "unknown" cannot be corrected
# without becoming nullable.
# Omitting the key instead (the route #3424 took for AuditLogEntry.
# response_time_ms, which raises no ERR because the schema declares no required
# list) was considered and rejected: #3424 itself drew the line at aggregates
# versus rows, emitting an explicit null from /audit/summary and /audit/report
# so a consumer of all three audit surfaces writes ONE optional-float model.
# This is the third of those three, and #3433 asks for that parity by name.
# Impact is bounded and checked: nothing in this org reads this endpoint's
# latency. The portal UI does not call session-summary at all (it appears only
# in orchestrator_proxy_allowlist.go as a permitted proxy route), no SDK,
# example or plugin references it, and its only in-repo consumers are
# runtime-e2e/2759_session_summary and runtime-e2e/2991_audit_read_scope_ux.
# Of those, only 2759 reads the latency at all, and only 2759 is changed here;
# 2991 calls the endpoint solely to check read scope and asserts nothing about
# avg_latency_ms, so it needed no update and correctly does not appear in this
# PR's diff. (An earlier draft of this entry said "both updated in this PR",
# which was untrue of 2991. The bound is unchanged - this file is what a future
# reviewer reads to re-derive a breaking change's blast radius, so the census
# has to be checkable against the diff rather than merely reassuring.)
# A client that cannot accept null can key on the new
# latency_sample_count (0 exactly when the average is null) instead of on the
# value. #3254 remains the standing SDK-model null-tolerance audit.
in API GET /api/v1/audit/session-summary the response property `buckets/items/avg_latency_ms` became nullable for the status `200`
in API GET /api/v1/audit/session-summary the response property `buckets/items/tools/items/avg_latency_ms` became nullable for the status `200`

# PR axonflow-enterprise#3443 (#3435) - SEBI compliance_score becomes nullable.
# Same class, and the same reasoning, as the #3429 avg_latency_ms entry above:
# a number that cannot express "unknown" cannot be corrected without becoming
# nullable. The score is derived from the violations the export actually read,
# so on an export where a section could not be produced - or was produced under
# a tenancy scope that cannot reach its rows - it has no basis, and 100.00 was
# an affirmative regulatory claim manufactured out of a read that did not
# happen. Measured on a live stack: the production-default portal shape
# reported "# Status,completed" and "# Compliance score,100.00" over a
# policy-violations section marked enabled_empty, on a database holding a real
# high-severity blocked prompt injection.
# Impact is bounded and checked. The ONLY consumer of POST
# /api/v1/sebi/audit/export in this org is the Enterprise customer portal
# (ee/platform/customer-portal-ui startSEBIAuditExport, proxied via
# orchestrator_proxy_allowlist.go:132), which ships in lockstep with the
# orchestrator; its SEBIAuditExportResponse type does not carry `summary` at
# all, so it never read the field. No SDK, example or plugin reads it, and
# that was CHECKED rather than assumed. THE COUNT IN THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG AND IS
# CORRECTED (#3435 R7): `grep -rn compliance_score examples/ sdk/` returns THREE
# hits, not one, and sdk/ contributes none of them. All three are unrelated to
# this endpoint, so the conclusion stands, but a waiver that cites a number
# anyone can falsify in one command discredits itself:
#   examples/support-demo/backend/main.go:135      the demo's OWN DashboardStats
#                                                  struct, served by its own backend
#   examples/support-demo/frontend/src/App.js:757  that same demo's frontend
#                                                  rendering that same struct
#   examples/indonesia-compliance/http/ojk-audit-export.sh:120
#                                                  reads compliance_score from
#                                                  GET /api/v1/ojk/dashboard, a
#                                                  different endpoint's field
# None of the three calls /api/v1/sebi. A client that cannot accept absence can
# key on `report_state`, which is `partial` or `not_available` exactly when the
# score is withheld. The companion additions in the same schema (report_state,
# sections, scope_gap, section_row_total, overlapping_records, scope_key) are
# additive and raise no ERR.
#
# NO ENTRY IS ADDED for the enum corrections in the same PR, and that was
# verified rather than assumed: oasdiff classifies
# response-property-enum-value-added as WARN and
# response-property-enum-value-removed as INFO, the workflow is `fail-on: ERR`,
# and ProcessIgnoredBackwardCompatibilityErrors only consults this file for
# ERR-level changes, so a line for either would be dead text.
#
# RECORD THE RAW DIFF, NOT THE POST-IGNORE ONE (#3435 R8). An earlier version
# of this note recorded "6 changes: 0 error, 6 warning, 0 info" as though it
# were the diff. It was the output WITH THIS FILE APPLIED, so the note read as
# "there is no error here" while sitting directly above the line that waives
# one. A waiver that quotes a clean number is arguing against its own
# existence.
#
# The invariant to re-derive, which does not drift as main moves:
#
#   oasdiff breaking base revision
#     -> EXACTLY ONE error, and it is response-property-became-nullable on
#        summary/compliance_score: the entry at the bottom of this block, and
#        the only reason this block exists. Everything else is WARN.
#
#   oasdiff breaking base revision --err-ignore .github/oasdiff-err-ignore.txt
#     -> ZERO errors. The workflow is `fail-on: ERR`, so this is the gate.
#
# Measured against origin/main while preparing this PR: 15 changes / 1 error /
# 14 warning raw, and 14 changes / 0 error / 14 warning with the ignore. Treat
# the counts as a sample and the two statements above as the contract.
#
# None of the warnings needs an entry: `status` gaining `partial`;
# `compliance_status` gaining `UNKNOWN` across its five reference sites;
# `SEBIComplianceCheck.status` and the OJK readiness check gaining `unknown`;
# and the removal of `SEBIComplianceCheck.message` and of `org_id` from
# SEBIRetentionResponse and SEBIExportMetadata, all three of which are
# properties the server has never emitted, and all of which land as
# response-optional-property-removed (WARN). Every one of these enums
# previously listed values the server has never emitted (`pending`,
# `processing`, `WARNING`) or omitted ones it emits routinely (`partial`,
# `UNKNOWN`, `unknown`), so a generated strict client could not deserialise the
# COMMON response on a stock deployment.
in API POST /api/v1/sebi/audit/export the response property `summary/compliance_score` became nullable for the status `200`
